subject: POC perf gates & evaluation plan — latency/throughput/cost/quality
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@pinecrestanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & proposed POC gates (latency / throughput / cost / quality)

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed evaluation plan so we can lock the POC scope and owners. Please review and call out any changes.

High-level objective
- Validate that Redwood Inference can serve Pinecrest’s \"user-query\" workload with production-grade latency, throughput, predictable unit economics, and no drop in quality for key intents.

Proposed success gates (acceptance criteria)
1) Latency (user-facing): p95 end-to-end response time <= 200 ms for 99% of queries during normal traffic profile (see sample_prompts.csv).
2) Throughput: support sustained 450 requests/sec with <= 10% tail-latency increase from baseline under the same request mix.
3) Cost / unit economics: average cost/token <= $0.0006 measured over the evaluation window (tokens counted per Redwood billing definition).
4) Quality: human-rated relevance >= 4.3/5 on a randomized sample of 200 queries OR automated intent-match >= 88% (we'll use the labeled eval set you provide).

Evaluation plan (phases & owners)
- Prep (week 0): Pinecrest provides a representative eval set and target query mix (owner: Elena). Redwood sends POC template and baseline harness (owner: Aditya). Attach: pinecrest_poc_template.xlsx, sample_prompts.csv.
- Baseline (week 1): Redwood runs baseline on sample set and shares perf/cost baseline (owner: Aditya).
- Trial window (weeks 2–3): Run live-style traffic against candidate model variants; collect latency/throughput/cost/quality metrics and human-review sample (owner: Marissa + Pinecrest reviewers).
- Review & decision (end of week 3): Joint review call to accept/reject POC based on gates.

Proposed timeline (flexible)
- Kickoff call: Mon Mar 22
- Baseline perf report: by Apr 1
- Evaluation window: Apr 5–Apr 19
- Decision review: Apr 26

Open questions / asks for you
- Confirm that the latency target above (p95 <= 200 ms) is acceptable — you mentioned 150ms on the call, but given network/proxy variance we propose 200ms as the initial gate.
- Share the labeled eval set and a prioritized list of intents by Mar 19.
- Let us know procurement contact for SOW/PO next steps.

If this looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff and loop in our infra team for a preshift.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

--
Attachments: pinecrest_poc_template.xlsx (POC template), sample_prompts.csv (sample query mix)
From: Elena Park <elena@pinecrestanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Frank Liu <frank.liu@pinecrestanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed POC gates (latency / throughput / cost / quality)

Thanks Jonas — this is a helpful summary. A few quick notes from our side: 

- Latency: we heard 150ms p95 as a stretch target during the call. Our infra team says 200ms p95 is acceptable for an initial pass; if we hit 200ms we will evaluate whether a 150ms SLA is warranted later.
- Throughput: 450 rps is in the right ballpark. Can you clarify whether this is sustained at peak or average? We prefer a sustained 450 rps at our expected concurrency.
- Cost/token: we need a short explanation of Redwood's token definition (what counts as a token and how system vs user tokens are billed). Please include that in the kickoff doc.
- Quality: we can provide a labeled set of 500 queries with intent labels; Frank will coordinate the dataset and the procurement side.

We also have a couple of constraints: the evaluation must run within our VPC (private deployment) for compliance, and we’ll need an exportable audit log for every request during the window. Is Redwood able to provide that?

If yes to the above, confirm kickoff Mar 22 and send the updated plan with role/owner table.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of ML, Pinecrest Analytics
elena@pinecrestanalytics.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed POC gates (latency / throughput / cost / quality)

Elena — great notes, thanks. Short answers and an updated owner matrix below. Also attached a short eval plan (redwood_eval_plan.pdf) that defines measurement methodology.

Answers / clarifications
- Throughput definition: the 450 rps target is a sustained rate (avg) over a 10-minute rolling window representative of peak traffic. We’ll simulate your production concurrency in the baseline run.
- Token definition / billing: Redwood bills on model input+output tokens as counted by the tokenizer used in the model runtime. System tokens (tooling, metadata) are included if they flow through the model; framing text we add is accounted for. For the POC we will provide a per-query token breakdown in the baseline report.
- VPC/private deployment: yes — Redwood Private supports evaluation inside your VPC and can stream audit logs to an S3 bucket or your logging endpoint. We’ll provide request-level traces and token counts for the window.

Updated owner matrix
- Pinecrest: provide labeled eval set + prioritized intents (owner: Elena).
- Pinecrest: procurement point (owner: Frank).
- Redwood SE: baseline perf & cost report, infra setup for VPC evaluation (owner: Aditya).
- Redwood CS: qualitative review and human rating coordination (owner: Marissa).
- Redwood AM: overall project coordination and decision backlog (owner: Jonas).

Proposed evaluation measurements (how we evaluate each gate)
- Latency: measure p50/p95/p99 over the evaluation window using real query mix; p95 <= 200 ms required.
- Throughput: run sustained load tests that mirror your concurrency distribution; throughput gate is avg sustained 450 rps with tail-latency change <= 10%.
- Cost/token: baseline report will show token counts + per-token cost; we’ll compute mean cost/token across the sample; gate: mean <= $0.0006.
- Quality: Redwood will run automated intent-match on labeled set and sample 200 responses for human rating; gate is human-rated >= 4.3/5 OR intent-match >= 88%.

Next steps (I’ll do these by EOD)
- Send kickoff invite for Mar 22 (30–45 min).
- Share redwood_eval_plan.pdf and an SOW template for procurement.
- Aditya will start infra onboarding prep for VPC connectivity.

Let me know if you want to nudge any gate numbers tighter before kickoff — happy to discuss.

Best,
Jonas

--

Elena
